_: Shared vocabulary merged into every adapter by adapters.load(). Methods are JS templates; adapters.plan() substitutes {{SEL}} / {{VAL}} (already JSON-encoded literals) and prepends js_helpers. javascript_tool REPL rule: the last expression is the return value, so never write a top-level `return`. Every template is a bare async IIFE with NO leading top-level `await` - the tool awaits the returned promise, and this form works on both javascript_tool implementations.

react_set.use: React-controlled <input>/<textarea> (Greenhouse, Ashby, Workday, LinkedIn). el.value='x' alone is silently discarded by React.

plain_set.use: Server-rendered plain HTML (Lever). Direct assignment works; events still dispatched so any jQuery listener sees it.

react_select.use: react-select combobox (Greenhouse dropdowns). Setting the visible input does NOT commit a selection - the listbox option must be clicked. Falls back to ArrowDown if filtering yields nothing.

select_by_text.use: Real <select>. Matches by visible option text, then sets by option value. Routes through jQuery when present so a select2 (Lever) repaints its visible label; a bare value set leaves select2 stale.

radio_pick.use: Radio group. {{SEL}} must select the whole group (e.g. input[name=cards\[uuid\]\[field2\]]). Matches on value first, then on the radio's own label text.

checkbox_set.use: Single checkbox. Clicks only when the current state differs, so it is idempotent on retry.

button_pick.use: Yes/No or multi-choice rendered as buttons (Ashby). {{SEL}} is the field CONTAINER. Click the button; never poke the hidden checkbox behind it - React owns that state.

autocomplete_pick.use: Typeahead that must resolve to a real suggestion (Ashby location, Lever location). A raw value set leaves the field unresolved and the form rejects it.

workday_prompt.use: Workday has NO <select> elements. {{SEL}} is the button[data-automation-id=...]; it opens a popup of [data-automation-id=promptOption] items that must be clicked.

file.use: Every platform here hides a REAL <input type=file> behind its dropzone. read_page (which returns non-visible nodes) or find -> ref -> mcp file_upload({tabId, ref, paths:[abs_path]}). NEVER click a file input or its Attach button: that opens an invisible native OS picker you cannot drive. javascript_tool cannot help - it cannot construct a File from a local path.

type_keys.use: Fallback when javascript_tool is unavailable/blocked: computer{left_click, ref} then computer{type}. Real keystrokes satisfy React without any JS. Slower; do not use for 100/day throughput unless the JS path fails.

profile_keys._: Canonical keys adapters.plan() reads out of profile.json. Anything not listed is a per-job override passed in job['overrides'].

work_auth_invariant.rule: authorized_to_work == 'Yes' AND requires_sponsorship == 'Yes', asserted together, read verbatim from profile.json. Never inferred, never model-generated. plan() raises if the pair is anything else.
work_auth_invariant.why: F-1 with CPT/OPT eligibility is lawfully authorized (NACE guidance) but will need H-1B after OPT expires. Answering 'No' to sponsorship is the single most common misrepresentation and surfaces at I-9 time.
wording_traps: 'authorized to work WITHOUT sponsorship' / 'unrestricted' / 'permanent basis' -> No (key: authorized_without_sponsorship)
'Are you a US citizen or permanent resident?' -> No (key: us_citizen_or_pr). Never answer Yes: a false claim to US citizenship is 18 U.S.C. 911 and a permanent inadmissibility bar.

answer_rules._: Ordered. First pattern (case-insensitive regex, tested against the discovered question label) wins. kind tells the agent which value shape to send; key names the profile value. kind=human -> stop and queue for a person. kind=fraud -> ABORT the whole application and flag.

rules.pattern: social security|\bssn\b|date of birth|\bdob\b|passport (number|no\b)|bank account|routing number|driver'?s licen[cs]e number
rules.why: Pre-offer request for identity/financial data. Abort and flag; never store or supply these.

Certification WITH a penalty clause ('false statements are grounds for dismissal') goes to a person. A plain 'I certify ... true and accurate' box is NOT caught here and still reaches `acknowledge` (pinned test). Sits first because the paragraph's EEO sentence would otherwise hit the gender/race rules. Also covers the HARD STOP 'I personally completed this application' (misstatement = grounds for discharge).

rules.pattern: security clearance|export control|export administration|\bear\b|\bitar\b|citizenship (status|requirement)|are you a (us|u\.s\.) citizen|permanent resident|permanent residency|u\.?s\.? person
rules.why: Citizenship-gated req. Answer is No but the role is usually disqualifying - let a person decide before submitting. 2026-09-01: `itar` was unanchored and matched inside 'military', so 'Are you a Veteran or an active member of the military?' resolved here instead of eeoc_veteran. Now \bitar\b.

rules.pattern: without\b.{0,40}?\b(sponsor\w*|(employer|company|visa|immigration)\s+support)|unrestricted (work )?authori[sz]ation|permanent basis|now or in the future.*without|without any restriction|without restriction|for any employer without|any employer without any|(?:for|by)\s+(?:all|any)\s+employers?|no restrictions|permanent (work )?authori[sz]ation|permanently authori[sz]ed
rules.why: NEGATIVE-POLARITY work-auth question -> answered from the frozen 'No' family. MUST stay ahead of authorized_to_work. 'Authorized to work for ANY employer WITHOUT ANY restrictions?' is NOT the same question as 'authorized to work in the US?' - F-1/OPT IS restricted, so mapping it to the positive rule produces a materially false statement on a federal-adjacent form.

rules.pattern: require.*sponsor(ship)?\b|need.*sponsor(ship)?\b|sponsor(ship)?.*(now|future)|visa sponsor(ship)?\b|require.{0,25}assistance with work authorization|sponsor you for a (work|visa)|sponsor\w*.{0,30}h-?1b|h-?1b.{0,25}(sponsor|petition|status\?)|require .{0,15}work authori[sz]ation|need .{0,15}work authori[sz]ation
legally authori[sz]ed|authori[sz]ed to (lawfully |legally )?work|authori[sz]ation to work|eligible to work|work authorization|legally allowed to work|allowed to work in the (us|u\.s\.|united states)
languages? (do you|you) speak|fluent in|language proficiency|which languages|^language(s)? fluency\*?$|^languages?\*?$

rules.why: MUST sit before source_of_referral: 'If you were referred by an employee, what is their name?' matched the referral-source rule and would type 'Website' into a person's NAME field. There is no referrer in profile.json, so this key resolves to nothing and the field is correctly left blank/routed rather than filled with the wrong value.

rules.pattern: how did you (first )?(hear|learn)|where did you hear|how you heard|tell us how you heard|referral source|source of (referral|application|hire)|referr(al|ed by)|where did you find
do you have (a |an )?notice period|restrictions on your availability
rules.why: MUST precede earliest_start_date, whose pattern contains 'notice period' and 'availability'. This phrasing is a Yes/No, so that rule would have written a DATE into a boolean field.

rules.pattern: ^(?!.*(?:currently (based|resid|liv|locat)|do you (currently )?live (in|near)|are you (currently )?(based|located|living) (in|near)|based near)).*?(?:willing to relocate|relocat|willing to commute|able to commute)
rules.why: Willingness only. Refuses labels containing a present-tense residency FACT ('are you currently based near our hub offices and able to commute 3 days/week') - for a candidate not based there, a blanket Yes is a false location claim. Those route to a human/judgment instead.

rules.pattern: ^(?!.*(?:currently (based|resid|liv|locat)|do you (currently )?live (in|near)|are you (currently )?(based|located|living) (in|near)|based near)).*?(?:(hybrid|onsite|on-site|in[- ]office|in the office).{0,80}(day|days|policy|requirement|week)|(day|days)\s*(a|per|/)\s*week.{0,60}(office|hybrid|onsite)|\d+x\s*(/|a|per)?\s*week.{0,60}(office|hybrid|onsite)|(office|hybrid|onsite).{0,60}\d+x\s*(/|a|per)?\s*week|anchor days|willing to relocate|relocate to|relocation|come into (a |the )?(our )?office|work from (our|the) (us |u\.s\. )?office|able to work.{0,40}(days?|onsite|hybrid|office)|comfortable.{0,30}(onsite|on-site|in[- ]office|hybrid)|(onsite|on-site|in[- ]office|hybrid) (setting|environment|role|position)|able and willing to work (onsite|on-site|in[- ]office)|(able|willing) to (work|be) (onsite|on-site|in[- ]office))
rules.why: Willingness only. Refuses labels containing a present-tense residency FACT ('are you currently based near our hub offices and able to commute 3 days/week') - for a candidate not based there, a blanket Yes is a false location claim. Those route to a human/judgment instead.

rules.pattern: what (u\.?s\.?|us) state|which (u\.?s\.?\s*)?state|state or (canadian )?province|state (you|of) residen|^state\*?$|state where you (currently )?(reside|live)
rules.why: MUST sit before the location rule: 'What U.S State do you currently reside in?' matches (reside) and would put 'Los Angeles, CA' into a state dropdown, which yields NO_OPTION. Source is identity.state.

rules.pattern: previously (worked|been employed)|ever (worked|been employed) (for|at|by)|former employee|previously applied|^\s*(are|have|did|do|were|was)\s+you\b.{0,80}(employed\s+(by|here|there|at|with)|an?\s+employee|employee\s+(here|there|of|at)|consultant|work(ed)?\s+(here|there|for us|at us|at this|at our))

rules.why: LinkedIn/Greenhouse numeric-validated free text - the single biggest source of failed submissions. Must be digits only.
Which degree you hold (a select). Deliberately does NOT match yes/no phrasings like 'Do you have a college degree?' - a bare 'degree' pattern used to type the full degree name into a Yes/No widget.

rules.pattern: year in school|current year in (school|your program)|class year|what year are you in
rules.why: MUST sit before the school rule, which matched 'select your current year in school' and would feed the school NAME into a year select. No profile key: derive from education[0].start or route to a human.

rules.pattern: current (company|employer)|company you work|current\s*/\s*(last|previous|prior) (company|employer)|current or (most recent|last|previous|prior) (company|employer)|who is your current
preferred (first )?name|preferred given name|goes by|nickname|name you go by
rules.why: MUST sit before the first_name rule: 'first name|given name' also matches 'Preferred First Name', which would write the legal first name into the preferred-name field.

MUST sit before first_name, for the same reason preferred_name does: 'Please list legal first and last name' matches 'legal first' and would write only the first name into a field asking for the whole name.
Late on purpose: the school / current-employer / referral rules above already claim the 'name of ...' labels.
Digits only. Portals that want E.164 declare the field explicitly (Greenhouse) instead of reaching this rule.
Must precede the eeoc_gender rule: 'preferred gender pronouns' contains 'gender' and would otherwise be answered 'Decline to self-identify' in a free-text pronoun field.

rules.pattern: sex assigned at birth|assigned sex|birth sex
rules.why: MUST precede eeoc_gender, whose pattern is a bare \bsex\b. Sex assigned at birth and gender identity are different questions with different answers for many people; conflating them writes an answer the user never gave.

rules.pattern: sexual orientation|do you identify as lgbt|lgbtq
rules.why: Added 2026-09-01; previously matched nothing and fell to the human queue.
2026-09-10: length-guarded (<=200 chars) so a legal paragraph whose EEO clause says "race, sex" cannot land here; (?<!trans) keeps "transgender" out.

MUST precede eeoc_race, whose pattern also contains 'hispanic|latino' as a bare alternative. Race and Hispanic/Latino ethnicity are DIFFERENT questions with independent answers in profile.json; answering one from the other is an inference, not the user's answer. Found live: 'Are you Hispanic/Latino?' resolved to eeoc_race and would have written the race value into an ethnicity question.
2026-09-10: length-guarded (<=200 chars) so a legal paragraph whose EEO clause says "race, sex" cannot land here.

Consent-to-AI-screening checkbox, increasingly required. Pattern now REQUIRES consent/acknowledge language next to the AI term - a bare mention of 'AI' (e.g. 'Which best describes how you use AI tools today?') must NOT match, since that is a usage question, not a consent.

rules.pattern: top (choice|preference)|first choice|only (firm|company|role) (you|i) (am|are) apply|(will |shall )?not apply to (any )?other|may not apply to other|exclusiv(e|ity)|no outstanding offers|have not (applied|interviewed) (to|with|at) any other
rules.why: MUST precede the `acknowledge` blanket-agree rule, which matches on 'acknowledg' and would otherwise tick this. The `acknowledge` key covers TERMS -- privacy notices, T&Cs, certifications, arbitration. This is not terms: it is a factual claim about the user's preferences that forecloses every other req at that firm for the season. Deliberately has NO _MAP entry, so it stays unanswered and routes to the user.

rules.pattern: cover letter|why (do you want|are you interested)|tell us|additional information|anything else

answer_rules.unmatched_why: Fail closed. A screening question nobody mapped is answered by a person, never guessed by the model.

fraud_scan.why: HARD RULE: a pre-offer form asking for SSN / DOB / passport / bank details is a fraud tripwire. Abort the application and flag it; do not fill anything.
fraud_scan.js: (async()=>{const bad=/social security|\bssn\b|date of birth|\bdob\b|passport (number|no\b)|bank account|routing number|driver'?s licen[cs]e number/i;const hits=[...document.querySelectorAll('label,legend,h1,h2,h3')].map(e=>__txt(e)).filter(t=>t&&bad.test(t));return hits.slice(0,5)})()

captcha_scan.why: All six platforms use an invisible/passive captcha that fires at submit. The anchor iframe is ALWAYS present and is not a blocker; only a VISIBLE challenge frame is. Detection only - solving or bypassing a captcha is out of scope, permanently.
captcha_scan.js: (async()=>{const f=[...document.querySelectorAll('iframe')].filter(i=>/recaptcha\/(api2|enterprise)\/bframe|hcaptcha\.com.*(challenge|hcaptcha-challenge)/i.test(i.src||''));const vis=f.filter(i=>{const r=i.getBoundingClientRect();if(r.width<80||r.height<80)return false;let n=i;for(let d=0;d<4&&n;d++,n=n.parentElement){const s=getComputedStyle(n);if(s.visibility==='hidden'||s.display==='none'||s.opacity==='0')return false}return true});const txt=document.body.innerText||'';if(vis.length)return'CAPTCHA_CHALLENGE';if(/verify you are human|complete the (security )?check|unusual traffic/i.test(txt))return'CAPTCHA_TEXT';return'ok'})()

step_ops.read_page: mcp read_page({tabId, filter:'interactive'}) - re-anchor refs after any DOM change
step_ops.js: mcp javascript_tool({tabId, text}) - returns the last expression; compare against step.expect
step_ops.file_upload: read_page/find -> ref for step.selector -> mcp file_upload({tabId, ref, paths:[step.path]}). <10MB total. Never click the input.
step_ops.discover: js step whose result is the question inventory; then apply answer_rules to each label
step_ops.verify: js step returning {key: readback}. Fail closed: any MISSING or mismatch on a required field -> human_queue, do NOT submit.
step_ops.abort_if: js step; if step.abort_when holds, stop and route per step.on_abort
step_ops.submit: NEVER emitted inside steps. Returned separately and requires explicit per-application human go-ahead in chat.

batching.how: One browser_batch per phase, ref-addressed actions only (form_input / file_upload / computer{left_click,ref}). Coordinates inside a batch aim at the PRE-batch screenshot and are stale - never batch coordinate clicks. Batches stop on first error. End each batch with read_page to re-anchor.
batching.waits: There is no wait-for-selector tool. Use the __wait poll already baked into the method JS; computer{action:'wait'} is a blind sleep of last resort.
